item.title: AI‑Generated Virus Blueprints Discussed by MIT Technology Review Innovator Samuel King
item.description:
AI‑Generated Virus Blueprints Discussed by MIT Technology Review Innovator Samuel King

In a subscriber‑only roundtable recorded on October 16 2026, MIT Technology Review’s senior AI reporter James O’Donnell speaks with Stanford bioengineering PhD candidate Samuel King about his 2025 work using a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses.

🔍 Overview

  • The conversation is part of MIT Technology Review’s “Roundtables” series.
  • It is available only to MIT Technology Review subscribers.
  • Listeners can watch the video or listen to the audio.

🧬 AI‑Generated Virus Blueprints

  • In 2025 Samuel King used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses.
  • The work addresses the question “Can AI design new life forms?”.
  • It is not yet an example of AI‑generated life, but could be next.

🎙️ Interview Details

  • Speakers: James O’Donnell (AI Reporter) and Samuel King (Bioengineering PhD Candidate, Stanford University/Arc Institute).
  • King was named one of MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35.
  • The session discusses new ways of seeing biology.

📅 Recording Information

  • Recorded on Friday, October 16, 2026.

⚠️ Context

  • “Don’t be fooled—LLMs don’t reason.”
  • “Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.”
  • “AI agents are not yet creative enough to carry out genuinely innovative open‑ended AI research, it seems.”
  • “Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities fall apart pretty quickly under scrutiny.”

#AI #Bioengineering #MITTechnologyReview #InnovatorsUnder35

Source: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses

item.title: Investigation Finds AI Surveillance Towers Failed to Prevent Border Deaths
item.description:
Investigation Finds AI Surveillance Towers Failed to Prevent Border Deaths

An investigation by MIT Technology Review has documented that over a thousand people died in areas monitored by US border surveillance towers, including those equipped with AI technology.

🔍 Overview

Over the last 25 years, the US has invested billions of dollars into a “virtual wall” of surveillance towers along the southern border. These towers were intended to:

  • Detect and apprehend border crossers
  • Save lives

⚙️ Key details

Despite the investment, the MIT Technology Review investigation found that over a thousand people moved through these watched areas without being apprehended or reached, ultimately resulting in their deaths. Some of these individuals were under the watch of AI-powered towers designed to spot people automatically.

#AI #Surveillance #BorderSecurity #MITTechnologyReview

Source: Roundtables: The Deadly Failures of The Virtual Border Wall

item.title: MIT Technology Review Investigation Finds Failures in Border Surveillance Towers
item.description:
MIT Technology Review Investigation Finds Failures in Border Surveillance Towers

An investigation by MIT Technology Review has documented that over a thousand people died in areas monitored by U.S. southern border surveillance towers without being reached or apprehended.

🔍 Overview

Over the past 25 years, the US has invested billions of dollars into a “virtual wall” of surveillance towers along the southern border. These towers were intended to:

  • Detect border crossers
  • Apprehend border crossers
  • Save lives

⚙️ Key details

Recent updates to the surveillance infrastructure include the installation of AI-powered towers. These specific towers are designed to spot people automatically; however, the investigation found that some individuals who died were under the watch of these AI-powered systems.

#AI #Surveillance #BorderSecurity #MITTechnologyReview

Source: Roundtables: The Deadly Failures of The Virtual Border Wall
